    if arr[mid] == target:
        result = mid

    elif arr[mid] < target:
        low = mid + 1

        if arr[mid] < x:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid

text: What is the worst-case time to search a rotated sorted array that may contain duplicates?
options: O(n), because when `arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high]` you cannot tell which half is sorted
O(log n), the same as without duplicates
answer: O(n), because when `arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high]` you cannot tell which half is sorted

text: Which fact makes O(log n) search possible in a rotated sorted array of distinct values?

At least one of the halves `[low, mid]` and `[mid, high]` is always sorted
The rotation point is always at index `n // 2`
answer: At least one of the halves `[low, mid]` and `[mid, high]` is always sorted

    low, high, count = 0, n - 1, 0
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        count += 1
        if mid == target:
            return count
        if mid < target:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid - 1
    return count
